authoring: Single-author synthetic confirmatory corpus; labels were not independently annotated.
relevanceRule: A candidate is relevant exactly when it is a different resolved incident with the same scenarioId as the source. Scenario IDs and relevance labels are metadata only and are never sent to PostgreSQL or included in searchable text.

incident.title: Archive restores omit recent customer documents
incident.description: Restored workspaces are missing files uploaded shortly before the nightly protection window. The original volume still contains the files and upload requests completed successfully.
incident.rootCause: The snapshot coordinator enumerated a stale manifest before asynchronous object writes had reached durable storage.
incident.fixApplied: Waited for the object-store completion watermark before sealing each snapshot manifest and repeated the affected backups.

incident.title: Point-in-time recovery is missing late-written blobs
incident.description: A recovery drill reconstructed database rows but referenced attachments were absent when uploaded near the backup boundary. Live reads continue to work.
incident.rootCause: Backup finalization recorded the object listing before multipart uploads were committed by the storage gateway.
incident.fixApplied: Added a commit barrier for pending multipart writes and verified restored attachment counts against the source.

incident.title: Workspace recovery drops files from the final upload batch
incident.description: Users recovered an older project tree even though upload audit entries show success. Missing items cluster at the end of the scheduled archive run.
incident.rootCause: The archive job closed its snapshot while background object acknowledgements were still outstanding.
incident.fixApplied: Drained the upload queue before snapshot closure and added a manifest-to-object reconciliation check.

incident.title: Backup image excludes attachments uploaded during rotation
incident.description: A tenant restored its content database but several recently submitted media files were not present in the generated image. No source objects were deleted.
incident.rootCause: Rotation advanced the active backup generation before the prior generation's blob copy completed.
incident.fixApplied: Made generation promotion wait for copy completion and rebuilt the affected backup images.

incident.title: Mobile push alerts arrive hours after dispatch
incident.description: Notifications remain queued even though the messaging vendor accepts requests normally. Delays are concentrated on devices that have not opened the app recently.
incident.rootCause: The token maintenance worker extended expired device registrations after comparing timestamps in local time.
incident.fixApplied: Normalized token expiry comparisons to UTC and removed registrations already rejected by the push provider.

incident.title: Dormant handset registrations block notification delivery
incident.description: A subset of users no longer receives mobile messages while active sessions receive them immediately. Provider logs mark many destination tokens as expired.
incident.rootCause: A cleanup task parsed provider expiry dates without their timezone offset and retained invalid registrations.
incident.fixApplied: Parsed RFC3339 expiry instants correctly, purged stale tokens, and retried pending alerts against current registrations.

incident.title: Background device cleanup leaves dead push endpoints
incident.description: The alert dispatcher spends most of its time retrying destinations that the vendor has already deactivated. Newly registered phones still work.
incident.rootCause: Expiry pruning used a server-local date boundary rather than the provider's UTC expiration timestamp.
incident.fixApplied: Switched pruning to UTC instants and added a metric for provider-invalid device tokens.

incident.title: Push queue backlog grows for inactive app users
incident.description: Message fanout succeeds for recently active clients but repeatedly targets stale handset addresses. The vendor reports those addresses are no longer registered.
incident.rootCause: A timezone-naive expiration conversion prevented old device tokens from being retired.
incident.fixApplied: Corrected expiration parsing and replayed queued notifications after deleting obsolete registrations.

incident.title: Analytics dashboards show duplicated daily totals
incident.description: Several reports nearly double-count activity after the overnight warehouse load. Source event identifiers are unique before ingestion.
incident.rootCause: The incremental loader resumed from a timestamp cursor without including a stable tie-break key, replaying rows at the page boundary.
incident.fixApplied: Changed the checkpoint to a composite timestamp and event identifier and removed duplicate warehouse rows.

incident.title: Nightly metrics inflate after warehouse job retries
incident.description: A transient worker restart causes a portion of yesterday's events to be counted twice in customer reports. Raw ingestion records have distinct IDs.
incident.rootCause: The batch checkpoint stored only the event time, so equal-time records were fetched again when a page retried.
incident.fixApplied: Persisted the last event ID with its timestamp and backfilled aggregates using a deduplicating merge.

incident.title: Warehouse activity counts repeat at pagination boundaries
incident.description: Daily usage charts jump after a delayed page is reprocessed. The upstream stream is append-only and no duplicate message was observed there.
incident.rootCause: An unstable incremental cursor sorted only by event timestamp and overlapped adjacent extraction pages.
incident.fixApplied: Added a deterministic identifier tie-break to the cursor and recomputed the affected reporting partitions.

incident.title: Customer usage report repeats events after resume
incident.description: Warehouse totals become overstated when an interrupted load continues from its saved position. The issue is limited to events sharing the same recorded time.
incident.rootCause: Resume state retained a timestamp but not the unique source sequence, making the extraction window overlap.
incident.fixApplied: Stored the source sequence alongside the timestamp and rebuilt the impacted daily summaries.

incident.title: Map tiles render as blank squares after regional rollout
incident.description: The map shell loads but tile requests return authorization failures only in one newly enabled geography. Existing regions and account credentials are healthy.
incident.rootCause: The edge policy replicated the region's public tile key without its matching host allowlist entry.
incident.fixApplied: Published the correct regional host policy and purged denied tile responses from the edge cache.

incident.title: New territory map backgrounds fail at the edge
incident.description: Users see an empty base layer while overlays and map controls remain available. Requests are rejected before reaching the tile origin.
incident.rootCause: The new CDN distribution omitted the tile service domain from its origin access policy.
incident.fixApplied: Added the tile origin to the regional edge allowlist and invalidated the failed authorization cache.

incident.title: Geographic imagery unavailable from newly provisioned CDN
incident.description: Only the recently launched region returns forbidden responses for background map imagery. The origin health check and user sessions are unaffected.
incident.rootCause: Edge configuration shipped with a stale permitted-host set that excluded the imagery endpoint.
incident.fixApplied: Corrected the host allowlist, synchronized the regional distribution, and cleared cached denials.

incident.title: Regional map layer disappears behind access-denied tiles
incident.description: The map canvas remains usable but raster tile URLs are blocked at the perimeter in one location. Requests in older locations continue to succeed.
incident.rootCause: A rollout copied the map API credential but not the corresponding CDN host authorization rule.
incident.fixApplied: Restored the regional edge rule and refreshed the tile distribution configuration.

incident.title: Invoice PDFs show garbled customer names
incident.description: Generated billing statements replace accented names with question marks while the customer profile page displays them correctly.
incident.rootCause: The document renderer selected a legacy font lacking the required glyphs and silently substituted characters.
incident.fixApplied: Bundled a Unicode-capable font family and regenerated statements produced during the affected release.

incident.title: Exported receipts corrupt non-English text
incident.description: Names containing diacritics are damaged in downloadable receipts but remain intact in the account database and web view.
incident.rootCause: The PDF template embedded a restricted Latin font and its fallback encoder dropped unsupported code points.
incident.fixApplied: Replaced the template font with a Unicode glyph set and validated multilingual receipt samples.

incident.title: Statement attachments lose accented letters
incident.description: Only the printed document differs from stored customer names; screen-rendered billing data is correct. The defect began after a template refresh.
incident.rootCause: The refreshed statement template used a font subset that omitted combining marks and extended characters.
incident.fixApplied: Embedded the full multilingual font subset and reissued affected statement files.

incident.title: Billing document renderer substitutes international glyphs
incident.description: PDF invoices contain replacement symbols for names with accents although database encoding checks pass and HTML invoices are unaffected.
incident.rootCause: The renderer's default typeface did not contain the requested Unicode glyphs and substitution occurred during PDF composition.
incident.fixApplied: Configured a Unicode font fallback chain and regenerated documents containing affected characters.

incident.title: Warehouse robots stop after battery swap
incident.description: A mobile picker becomes unreachable from dispatch shortly after its battery is replaced. The robot itself remains powered and reports a healthy radio.
incident.rootCause: The fleet agent cached the previous battery module's device identity and rejected the replacement's signed hardware claim.
incident.fixApplied: Refreshed device attestation on module change and re-enrolled the affected robot identities.

incident.title: Autonomous cart disappears from fleet control after service
incident.description: A serviced unit operates locally but no longer receives route assignments. Network connectivity is stable and the fleet gateway is available.
incident.rootCause: Hardware attestation remained bound to the removed power module after maintenance exchanged the battery pack.
incident.fixApplied: Invalidated cached module credentials during service and completed a fresh robot enrollment.

incident.title: Picker cannot rejoin control plane after power-pack replacement
incident.description: One autonomous warehouse vehicle is absent from the scheduling console after a battery change despite passing onboard diagnostics.
incident.rootCause: The device certificate referenced the former battery controller because the identity agent did not renew its attestation.
incident.fixApplied: Forced a new hardware claim on battery replacement and restored the vehicle to the dispatch fleet.

incident.title: Fleet scheduler rejects robot with swapped energy module
incident.description: Route planning excludes a single vehicle whose sensors and wireless signal are normal. The alert began immediately after routine equipment work.
incident.rootCause: Cached identity evidence still described the detached battery module, causing device attestation to fail.
incident.fixApplied: Cleared module-bound identity state, re-attested the robot, and added a maintenance-change hook.

incident.title: Laboratory spectrometer reports drifting calibration
incident.description: Readings slowly diverge from reference samples after repeated warm-up cycles. The sensor electronics and reference standard are stable.
incident.rootCause: Calibration coefficients were applied before the optics reached thermal equilibrium, biasing the stored baseline.
incident.fixApplied: Delayed calibration until temperature stabilized and recalibrated instruments that recorded premature baselines.

incident.title: Assay measurements wander between morning runs
incident.description: Quality controls pass initially but measured concentration shifts as the analyzer warms. External reference material shows no corresponding change.
incident.rootCause: The instrument saved a zero point while its optical chamber was still heating and later used that offset for all samples.
incident.fixApplied: Required a stable chamber-temperature window before zeroing and repeated runs with affected assay batches.

incident.title: Chemical analyzer baseline shifts after startup
incident.description: Laboratory results become progressively biased during the first operating hour although calibration fluid remains within specification.
incident.rootCause: The calibration routine captured dark-current and optical reference values before thermal settling completed.
incident.fixApplied: Added a warm-up stability check ahead of baseline capture and reprocessed samples from the unstable interval.

incident.title: Spectral instrument needs repeated recalibration each shift
incident.description: Technicians observe a consistent initial offset that shrinks after the device has been running for a while. The certified reference sample is unchanged.
incident.rootCause: The startup sequence calibrated optics before the enclosure reached its operating temperature.
incident.fixApplied: Moved calibration after thermal equilibrium and added a readiness indicator for laboratory operators.

incident.title: Parking gates charge drivers after they have exited
incident.description: Some sessions remain billable after a vehicle leaves the facility. Camera records confirm exit, but the payment ledger has no corresponding departure event.
incident.rootCause: The exit reader published events with a new controller sequence format that the session reconciler ignored.
incident.fixApplied: Accepted the updated sequence schema and reconciled open parking sessions against verified gate departures.

incident.title: Garage occupancy stays high after vehicles depart
incident.description: The management console shows cars still parked after they passed the exit barrier. Entry processing and payment capture are otherwise normal.
incident.rootCause: A firmware update changed the departure message field name and the occupancy consumer discarded those events.
incident.fixApplied: Updated the exit-event parser for the controller schema and corrected stale active parking sessions.

incident.title: Parking invoices include completed visits twice
incident.description: A subset of motorists receives an additional charge because the system still considers their first visit active after leaving the lot.
incident.rootCause: Gate departure notifications were not applied when the barrier firmware emitted its revised event envelope.
incident.fixApplied: Supported the new departure payload version and closed sessions using the gate controller's exit audit.

incident.title: Exit lanes fail to close parking transactions
incident.description: Vehicle departures are visible in the camera archive but parking records remain open and continue accruing fees after checkout.
incident.rootCause: The reconciliation service rejected exit messages produced by a newer lane-controller firmware release.
incident.fixApplied: Added compatibility for the new event envelope and settled the affected sessions from verified departure logs.
